claims.text: The proposed initial material is a rare-earth-free, approximately equiatomic Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has a fine-grained microstructure containing dispersed nanoscale precipitates.
Controlled heat treatment or adjustment of rapid-solidification parameters can systematically increase or refine the nanoscale precipitate population.
Controlled heat treatment or adjustment of rapid-solidification parameters can reduce the alloy's grain size.
Nanoscale precipitates, potentially Mn2O3-like particles, are concentrated at fine grain boundaries.
The relevant microstructure has a high dislocation density.
Nanoscale precipitates act as local stress concentrators.
Local stresses associated with the precipitates enhance magnetoelastic coupling.
Enhanced magnetoelastic coupling lowers the anisotropy-energy barriers for magnetic reorientation under low applied fields.
Lower magnetic-reorientation barriers produce a larger magnetocaloric entropy change at low applied fields.
The distribution of precipitates along fine grain boundaries promotes efficient heat exchange.
The distribution of precipitates along fine grain boundaries minimizes magnetic hysteresis.
High dislocation density contributes to mechanical robustness.
Increasing precipitate density and refining grains will increase the magnetocaloric entropy change relative to a conventionally processed baseline at low fields.
Increasing precipitate density and refining grains will produce a faster thermal response during cyclic magnetization.
Increasing precipitate density and refining grains will reduce magnetic hysteresis.
Increasing precipitate density and refining grains will maintain or improve mechanical strength.
The proposed mechanism applies only over a processing window in which precipitate coarsening or agglomeration is avoided.
Very high magnetic fields can activate magnetic mechanisms different from the proposed low-field mechanism.
The quantitative relationship between precipitate size or density and magnetocaloric response is not established.
